snippet.title: Stock Market Crash of 2008
snippet.description: This video shows the events of the 2008 financial recession. This event affected the whole world and cause major indices to fall about 40% from their highs and took several years to recover. This video is to show the dangers of investing and how no matter what low-risk stock you own, a crash of this magnitude has happened and can happen again so there is no such thing as a no-risk investment. Many companies went into bankruptcy, including bank giant Lehman Brothers, and many others were damaged for many years to come. The closest thing to the 1929 depression, the 2008 recession is the closest thing to the end of capitalism the United States has seen in the 21st century. I hope viewers can take away the notion that investing carries high risk, and you could lose everything if you are not diversified. snippet.title: Federal Reserve Economic Conditions of the United States (College Fed Challange)
snippet.description: This video is an overview of the economic conditions currently in the United States from the Federal Reserve Bank's data releases. The graphs in the presentation can be used to determine the state of the economy in the U.S and then predict the future actions the Federal Reserve Bank may take to correct it. These macroeconomic graphs can help predict trends and shows why the economy is acting the way it is. This was from my Federal Reserve Challenge in college and is a good baseline for those who want to make one.

snippet.title: Stock Market Crash of 2020 Coronavirus
snippet.description: This shows the sudden effects of the Cornavirus pandemic affecting the U.S economy and stock market. With the sudden swings and extreme volatility, this recent stock crash shows the use of circuit breakers, trading halts, and stock futures limit up and downs. When the pandemic entered the U.S, the health of the financial system was hit badly as well and this was the first pandemic to affect the economy in such a bad way since 1918. This video is meant to show the sudden rise in fear and panic selling, and how the quick month-long recovery shows that holding strong investments will always prevail.
